action_criteria.expected_evidence: Agrammatic telegraphic speech with apraxia of speech, spared single-word comprehension and object knowledge, from the daughter's history and the bedside screen
action_criteria.label: Structured language history and bedside screen scored against the Gorno-Tempini PPA features
action_criteria.rationale: The PPA variant is defined by which language features are impaired and which are spared.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Agrammatic production with apraxia of speech features, preserved single-word comprehension and object knowledge, preserved episodic memory and visuospatial function
action_criteria.label: Neuropsychological battery including language, motor speech, episodic memory, executive and visuospatial measures
action_criteria.rationale: Quantifies the production deficit and documents spared comprehension, memory and visuospatial function.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Apraxia of speech without dysarthria, agrammatic production with mildly impaired complex-sentence comprehension, intact word comprehension
action_criteria.label: Speech and language evaluation (motor speech, connected speech, grammar and syntactic comprehension, repetition, single-word comprehension, writing)
action_criteria.rationale: A formal motor speech and language assessment separates apraxia of speech and agrammatism from dysarthria and is the baseline for therapy and communication aids.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No metabolic, endocrine, nutritional or inflammatory cause of the decline
action_criteria.label: Reversible-cause blood tests: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, folate, ESR, CRP
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes metabolic, endocrine, nutritional and inflammatory contributors before attributing decline to neurodegeneration.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left posterior frontal and insular cortical thinning with normal DWI, excluding acute vascular event; posterior cortex and hippocampi preserved
action_criteria.label: MRI brain without contrast, dementia protocol
action_criteria.rationale: Shows the left posterior fronto-insular atrophy pattern and excludes a new infarct or other structural cause of the speech change.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Left posterior fronto-insular hypoperfusion or hypometabolism with preserved temporal and posterior cortex
action_criteria.label: Perfusion SPECT or FDG-PET when the structural picture is unresolved
action_criteria.rationale: Left posterior fronto-insular hypoperfusion or hypometabolism gives imaging support for the non-fluent variant when the atrophy is subtle.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on diagnostic criteria and management
action_criteria.label: Literature search on non-fluent/agrammatic primary progressive aphasia (optional background, not a clinical step)
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; nothing in the diagnosis or plan depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not attribute the progressive speech deficit to the prior TIA without new DWI evidence of ischemia: stroke-related aphasia stabilizes or improves, whereas this deficit worsens.
Do not start a cholinesterase inhibitor (donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine): no benefit in FTD, NICE NG97 advises against it, and it may worsen behaviour.
Do not start memantine: a randomised trial showed no benefit in FTD and NICE NG97 advises against it.
Do not order DaTscan in the absence of parkinsonism: no rigidity, bradykinesia, or supranuclear gaze palsy is present, and DaTscan does not distinguish nfvPPA from PSP-SPS.
required_recommendations: Apply the Gorno-Tempini 2011 criteria and name the variant: at least one core feature (agrammatism or apraxia of speech) and at least 2 of impaired complex-syntax comprehension, spared single-word comprehension and spared object knowledge.
Document the progressive course (18 months of worsening) that distinguishes a neurodegenerative aphasia from stroke-related aphasia, which plateaus or improves.
Confirm that single-word comprehension is intact to distinguish the non-fluent variant from svPPA, and that grammar and motor speech are affected to distinguish it from lvPPA.
Plan longitudinal review for emerging PSP or corticobasal features (falls, vertical gaze palsy, axial rigidity, limb apraxia, alien limb).
Refer for speech and language therapy and augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) planning to maintain communication as the syndrome progresses.

Address safety and support for living alone: a way to summon help without speech (text or alert device), caregiver education for her daughter, lasting power of attorney while she has capacity, and support for her social isolation.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG is non-specific in nfvPPA and not part of the PPA diagnostic pathway unless seizures or rapidly progressive course raises concern for CJD or autoimmune encephalitis.
ECG has no role in the workup of progressive aphasia and is not indicated absent cardiac symptoms.
Echocardiography evaluates cardiac structure and is unrelated to a progressive neurodegenerative language syndrome.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is unrelated to the diagnostic question and not indicated without cardiac symptoms.
DaTscan is not indicated in nfvPPA without overt parkinsonism; no rigidity, bradykinesia, or supranuclear gaze palsy present.
MR spectroscopy has no established role in the routine nfvPPA diagnostic pathway.
Carotid duplex evaluates extracranial vascular disease and has no diagnostic role once a progressive neurodegenerative language syndrome is identified.

differential.diagnosis: Progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) with speech predominant syndrome (SPS-PSP)
differential.key_features: For: apraxia of speech with agrammatism is a recognised PSP presentation. Against at this stage: no vertical gaze palsy, falls or axial rigidity; review longitudinally.

differential.diagnosis: Corticobasal syndrome (CBS) with dominant language phenotype
differential.key_features: Against: no limb apraxia, alien limb, myoclonus or cortical sensory loss on examination; review longitudinally.
Against: agrammatism and apraxia of speech, preserved episodic memory and posterior cortex; lvPPA has word-retrieval pauses and impaired sentence repetition without apraxia of speech.

differential.diagnosis: Ischemic stroke / TIA (new lacunar event in speech areas)
differential.key_features: For: prior TIA and the initial 'speech stroke' attribution. Against: DWI-negative MRI without a strategic infarct, and 18 months of progressive worsening rather than plateau or recovery.
Against: single-word comprehension and object knowledge are preserved, category fluency is preserved, and the temporal lobes are spared.

key_clinical_evidence: Agrammatic, telegraphic production with apraxia of speech, spared single-word comprehension and object knowledge, and spared episodic memory meet the Gorno-Tempini 2011 non-fluent variant criteria.
Progressive worsening over 18 months, reported by her daughter and the referring speech-language pathologist, distinguishes a neurodegenerative aphasia from post-stroke aphasia.
Left posterior frontal and insular atrophy on MRI, with a DWI-negative scan and no strategic infarct, argues against a vascular cause of the speech change.
The severe letter-fluency impairment with preserved category fluency is a production-based deficit, the opposite of the semantic variant.
PSP with speech-predominant presentation and corticobasal degeneration are the likely pathologies to watch for: no falls, supranuclear gaze palsy, axial rigidity or limb apraxia yet.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The prior TIA resolved completely four years before the current syndrome. An 18-month progressive language decline is inconsistent with a fixed stroke deficit; structural MRI shows the focal degenerative pattern.
red_herrings.data_point: Remote TIA 4 years ago and initial attribution of speech changes to 'stroke effects'
red_herrings.intended_effect: Prior TIA history prompts framing of halting speech as stroke-related dysarthria or post-ischemic aphasia, delaying recognition of a progressive neurodegenerative process.

Non-fluent/agrammatic primary progressiv.summary: Gorno-Tempini and colleagues (2011) define non-fluent/agrammatic PPA by agrammatism or apraxia of speech with at least two of impaired syntactic comprehension, spared single-word comprehension and spared object knowledge; imaging support is left posterior fronto-insular atrophy or hypometabolism. Progressive supranuclear palsy and corticobasal degeneration are common underlying pathologies.

metadata.notes: Straightforward nfvPPA — 69-year-old East Asian retired schoolteacher with 18-month progressive agrammatic/apraxic speech misattributed to stroke due to prior TIA. Key teaching: nfvPPA = production deficit with spared comprehension (opposite of svPPA); progressive course distinguishes from vascular aphasia; left posterior frontoinsular atrophy on MRI is the structural correlate.

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. C is a 69-year-old East Asian retired schoolteacher, widowed, referred to the neurology outpatient clinic by her speech-language pathologist after an 18-month course of progressive speech difficulty that initially failed to improve as expected following what the family physician had attributed to a 'speech stroke.' The patient has a history of a remote lacunar TIA four years ago from which she made a complete clinical recovery. Approximately 18 months ago, her adult daughter noticed that her mother — a lifelong Mandarin-English bilingual who had taught primary school for 35 years — was becoming increasingly effortful and telegraphic in conversation, producing shorter and shorter utterances with visible struggle and frequent sound errors. The family physician obtained a non-contrast head CT at that time, which was reported as normal, and attributed the speech changes to a possible new lacunar event that had been missed, maintaining her on aspirin. However, over the subsequent 18 months the speech difficulty has continued to worsen rather than plateau or improve. The patient produces only 2-4 word telegraphic utterances with effortful, halting articulation. She omits grammatical function words and auxiliaries. She makes consonant substitution errors. In contrast, her comprehension of spoken language is fully preserved at the single-word and object level: she correctly follows all multi-step commands during the visit, identifies pictures accurately, and demonstrates intact object knowledge. She can communicate in writing more fluently than orally. There is no behavioral change, no apathy, no disinhibition, no perseverative behavior, no change in appetite or food preferences, no incontinence, and no falls. Episodic memory is described as intact by her daughter. She independently manages her household and finances. She has become isolated because communication is increasingly distressing. The speech-language pathologist who referred her noted: 'Her speech has kept getting worse during therapy rather than recovering; please assess.'

neurological_exam.additional: Daughter reports an 18-month history of progressive difficulty with speech. Initially attributed by the family physician to 'effects of a mini-stroke' given the prior TIA history. The patient herself is aware and distressed by her communication difficulty. She uses compensatory strategies such as writing notes and gesture. Episodic memory appears relatively intact by informant report: she independently manages finances, medication scheduling, and calendar. No behavioral disinhibition, no apathy, no repetitive behaviors, no dietary changes reported. No falls. No hallucinations. No urinary symptoms. No swallowing difficulty.
neurological_exam.coordination: Intact finger-nose, heel-shin bilaterally. Normal rapid alternating movements. No dysmetria.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Cranial nerves II-XII intact. No dysarthria of cerebellar type. No lower motor neuron bulbar signs. Palate elevates symmetrically. Gag intact. Tongue midline, no fasciculations. Jaw jerk absent. No facial asymmetry. Eye movements full, no supranuclear gaze palsy, no hypometric saccades.
neurological_exam.gait: Normal cadence and stride length. Normal arm swing bilaterally. No parkinsonian features. Tandem gait intact. Romberg negative.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and cooperative. Anxious about speaking. Spontaneous speech markedly reduced in fluency and phrase length: produces 2-4 word telegraphic utterances with visible articulatory effort, frequent hesitations, and intermittent consonant substitutions (e.g., 'spook' for 'spoke'); omits auxiliary verbs and function words in longer phrases. Follows multi-step commands. Writing is telegraphic but better preserved than speech.
neurological_exam.motor: Normal bulk and tone bilaterally. Strength 5/5 throughout all muscle groups. No tremor, no rigidity, no bradykinesia. No alien-limb phenomenon. No limb apraxia on examination when verbal instructions are bypassed (patient can imitate pantomimed actions accurately).
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ symmetric throughout upper and lower extremities. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally. No Hoffmann sign. No primitive reflexes (palmomental, grasp, snout absent).
neurological_exam.sensory: Normal to light touch, pinprick, and proprioception bilaterally. No cortical sensory loss.
